svg.text: If it is the wrong project: six options, then worked examples (Figures 4-14 to 4-17)
Do it anyway
fine briefly (take one for the team) but know why and when it ends; if it saps you,
tell your manager plainly; you may have outgrown the team
Compensate
add a side project for what is missing; make space in the calendar; 'torch the back
burner' (Grace Vigeant)
Let others lead
Michael Lopp: aggressively delegate; they get a B and you coach toward an A; do not
take all the public wins
Resize
join for a month, consult, meet once, recommend someone else, care for the length
of a meeting
Just say no
not all problems are yours; borrow scripts and watch how admired colleagues
decline; an '#isaidno' label
Pay attention to 'I don't want to'
do not rationalise it; look for a variant that fits and tell your manager what kind
of work you want
All-hands talk after a draining 18-month project good visibility but costs
vacation and energy; ask if it is new for you, whether someone else needs it more,
or shorten, co-present or postpone
Joining the incident-commander rotation skill, credibility and capital boost; time
and energy cost; decide on quality of life now; try six months
The exciting project you cannot fit take it, but block its time in the calendar
first and talk to your manager about the process work
I want to want to great on paper, no appetite: listen to that; reshape (coach the
lead, join for a month) or decline
